nodes.text: Let $R(k,l)$ be the usual Ramsey number: the smallest $n$ such that if the edges of $K_n$ are coloured red and blue then there exists either a red $K_k$ or a blue $K_l$. Prove the existence of some $c>0$ such that\[\lim_{k\to \infty}\frac{R(k+1,k)}{R(k,k)}> 1+c.\]

#1030 : [Er93,p.339] graph theory | ramsey theory A problem of Erdős and Sós, who could not even prove whether $R(k+1,k)-R(k,k)>k^c$ for any $c>1$. It is trivial that $R(k+1,k)-R(k,k)\geq k-2$. Burr, Erdős, Faudree, and Schelp [BEFS89] proved\[R(k+1,k)-R(k,k)\geq 2k-5.\]See also [544] for a similar question concerning $R(3,k)$, and [1014] for the general off-diagonal case.
